# Azure Pipelines baseline E2E

## Requirements and approval

- User approved a YAML-only baseline E2E branch pushed directly to
  `Azure/fleet-networking`, named `ci/ado-e2e-baseline`.
- Start from upstream main, not the unrelated Service Gateway feature branch.
- Reuse `aks fleetnetworking` WIF and existing `DefaultAzureCredential` via
  Azure CLI. Do not change Go authentication or GitHub CI.
- Do not queue a pipeline or create/delete live Azure resources.
- The prior WIF smoke test succeeded in ADO build 191581304.

## Plan and success criteria

- [x] Inspect main's pipeline, provisioning, test, and cleanup paths.
- [x] Extend the manual pipeline for baseline shared-VNet only, with explicit
  runtime consent, expected subscription, unique RG, tools, bounded timeouts,
  WIF session refresh, diagnostic upload, and scoped cleanup.
- [x] Document branch execution, permissions, cleanup, and authentication limits.
- [x] Validate YAML, inline shell, and failure/cleanup behavior offline.
- Delivery: commit and push only this change, then verify the remote branch.

## Decisions

- Use an isolated worktree based on `origin/main` at `b48652c`.
- Keep AFD and Traffic Manager disabled. No Service Gateway code exists on this
  main-based branch.
- Run setup, tests, and cleanup in separately authenticated AzureCLI tasks.
  Force the existing default credential chain to select Azure CLI for tests.
- Use the task's experimental `keepAzSessionActive`, not a custom refresh loop.
  Live token refresh is not proven by offline checks.
- Require explicit approval of billable creation and cleanup at manual queue
  time as well as the externally managed service connection approval.

## Files and before/after

- `.pipeline/e2e-tests.yaml`: read-only smoke test becomes an opt-in baseline
  lifecycle; still no CI or PR triggers.
- `test/README.md`: directly related Azure Pipelines usage and limitations.
- This breadcrumb records approval and validation.

## Validation and unresolved risks

- Passed YAML parsing and `bash -n` for every inline script.
- Passed offline mocked setup cases: wrong subscription, existing RG, successful
  setup, and setup failure after recording that cleanup is needed.
- Passed offline mocked cleanup cases: wrong run name, absent RG, wrong source
  tag, wrong resource ID, successful deletion/wait, failed deletion, failed wait.
- Passed trigger/consent guards, explicit Azure CLI credential selection, cleanup
  conditions, artifact scope, and directly added relative-document link checks.
- Azure DevOps pipeline 489143 preview API successfully expanded the YAML with
  consent enabled. Preview did not queue a run or execute tasks.
- Organization task metadata confirms AzureCLI 2.282.3 exposes
  `keepAzSessionActive`; actual refresh is still unverified.
- No Go changes; no Go build or live E2E was needed for these YAML/docs changes.

No live execution is authorized. Azure role assignments, quota/policy acceptance,
agent entitlement, cancellation cleanup, and long-running WIF refresh require an
approved live run. AKS creation can itself require role-assignment privileges even
with Traffic Manager disabled; do not broaden the identity to Owner automatically.

## Follow-up: hosted-agent disk exhaustion (2026-11-17 UTC)

- Run 191586199 completed setup, then the agent failed with
  `System.IO.IOException: No space left on device` during the test step.
  Logs, artifact upload, and Azure cleanup were abandoned.
- User requested a fix. Scope stays on this branch: no rerun, no Azure cleanup,
  no Go/Dockerfile changes.
- [x] Add a run-specific builder name and remove that builder/cache between image
  publication and Go tests, without global pruning.
- [x] Add before/after disk diagnostics and remove the baseline's unnecessary
  five-minute role-propagation sleep.
- [x] Passed inline-script Bash syntax, mocked run-specific removal and error
  propagation, existing lifecycle guards, and Azure DevOps YAML preview.
- Retained Azure resources still need inspection and approved cleanup. Offline
  checks cannot establish the reclaimed byte count or live E2E success.
